title: Hib vaccine (Haemophilus influenzae type b)
what: The vaccine protects against a bacterium that in small children can cause meningitis and severe pneumonia. It is often given in one shot together with other vaccines.
why: For children under 5 on the schedule, and sometimes for older children and adults with certain illnesses.
duration: the shot takes a few seconds; with the check-up usually 15 to 40 minutes
tell_doctor: If your child is sick now or has a fever
Allergies and strong reactions to past vaccines

prepare.title: Health
prepare.text: The vaccine is given when your child is healthy. Your child will be examined before the shot.

prepare.title: Schedule
prepare.text: It is often part of a combined vaccine. Ask your pediatrician how many shots are needed.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Comfortable clothes that are easy to take off the leg or shoulder.

steps: The doctor examines your child and takes the temperature
The skin is wiped and the shot is given in the thigh or arm
The vaccine is recorded in the documents
After the shot, stay at the clinic for about 30 minutes
feel: A quick shot. Your child may cry for a bit
Sometimes redness at the spot or a mild fever
after: Stay near the office for 30 minutes
At home keep to the usual routine and offer more drinks
red_flags: Trouble breathing, a swollen face, a rash all over: call your local emergency number
High fever that does not come down: see a doctor

faq.q: If my child is already over one year old, is the vaccine still needed?
faq.a: Often fewer shots are enough. The pediatrician will choose the plan.

faq.q: Does it protect against all meningitis?
faq.a: No, only the kind caused by this bacterium. There are separate vaccines for others.

reminders.text: Your child's vaccine tomorrow. Bring the vaccination record.
